headline: Brent settled at 109.55 dollars after Houthi strikes on Saudi energy sites and a mined tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, keeping alive the inflation input that has held the US 10 year yield above 5 percent, even as chip stocks bounced and the Nasdaq added 1.11 percent.

summary.us: The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.11 percent to 26,430.89 and the S&P 500 added 0.41 percent to 7,690.73 as buyers returned to AI and chip names after the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell for eight straight sessions and shed roughly 2 trillion dollars of market value, while the Dow slipped about 0.07 percent. Reports credited easing oil prices and slightly lower Treasury yields for the bounce, though the 10 year is still above 5 percent and the week's real test is earnings from Netflix on Tuesday and Meta and Tesla on Wednesday.
summary.india: The Sensex fell 876.37 points or 1.17 percent to 73,852.90 and the Nifty closed at 22,888.95 as private banks dragged, with HDFC Bank down more than 2 percent after September quarter net profit grew only 4.7 percent and Axis Bank also missing expectations. Public sector banks went the other way on stronger results, with PNB up about 8 percent, while foreign institutions sold about 1,149 crore rupees of cash equities against roughly 3,201 crore rupees of domestic buying and the rupee firmed to around 94.70 to 94.85, its strongest in about six weeks.
summary.global: Asia was mixed as the Nikkei 225 fell 0.62 percent to 64,916.70 and the Shanghai Composite added about 0.39 percent to 3,730.92, with Hong Kong closed for Chung Yeung Day. Europe sold off, with the DAX down 1.18 percent, the FTSE 100 down 1.08 percent and the CAC 40 down 1.11 percent, as oil near 110 dollars and the global bond selloff that pushed the US 30 year yield to 5.715 percent weighed on risk appetite.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to the cost of money rather than the promise of AI. Hot September CPI and PPI prints pushed fed funds futures toward pricing another quarter point increase by year end, and with the 10 year above 5 percent the market stopped asking whether AI compute is wanted and started asking who funds it: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit a record, the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell for eight straight sessions, and the Nasdaq shed 4.48 percent on the week while the Dow, carried by defensives, held a 0.67 percent gain. India went the other way, with the Nifty adding 3.44 percent as IT earnings landed well and the rupee rallied for six sessions on RBI intervention, even as October foreign outflows neared 50,000 crore rupees. Commodities split sharply, with WTI up 7.83 percent on a large US inventory draw and Strait of Hormuz risk while silver dropped 5.83 percent and gold was little changed, and crypto drifted lower on continued spot ETF outflows and close to a billion dollars of leveraged liquidations. Next week brings the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO, the largest in Indian history, alongside Tesla and Netflix earnings, Infosys on Friday and flash PMIs, all inside the Fed blackout that runs to the 28 October decision.
